findings.symbol: src/capacity/api.py::_clamp_gate (the `falsified` clause, lines ~294-299, on the `if lifts:` arm)
findings.detail: NEW CODE, AND THE SENTENCE IS FALSE ON HALF THE ARMS IT IS APPENDED TO -- and their own repro quotes that exact case as a pass. The repair rewrote the UNREACHABLE headline from 'no lift can be earned at all' to 'NO LIFT CAN BE HELD AT A HARD CEILING', but left the falsification predicate keyed on the OLD claim: `falsified` is computed once from `dead_facts` alone and appended to BOTH the `if clamped:` (FIRED) and the `if lifts:` (armed, did-not-fire) returns. On the FIRED arm it is correct -- clamped > 0 does falsify 'no lift can be held at a ceiling'. On the lifts-only arm it is not: clamped == 0 means no lift was held at a ceiling, which is what the analysis said, so the ledger AGREES. The result is a single Gate reason that says both things: '7 earned lift(s) and every one was applied IN FULL -- no lift reached the hard ceiling ... THE STARTUP ANALYSIS SAID NO LIFT COULD BE HELD AT A CEILING HERE AND THE LEDGER DISAGREES'. This is the same self-contradiction class as finding 1, in the half of the change written to prevent 'two report lines disagreeing'. NOT REACHABLE IN THE TREE TODAY (CAP.counters raises NotImplementedError, so nothing rebuilds the gate with a live ledger) -- but _clamp_gate is on the frozen surface, the report's own repro invokes it, and P4 will. FIX THAT WEAKENS NOTHING: gate the clause on the event it is about -- compute `falsified` only when `clamped` is non-zero, and for the lifts-only arm say instead that the analysis's per-arm grounds are contradicted by lifts having been earned ('THE STARTUP ANALYSIS SAID NO LIFT COULD BE EARNED ON THESE ARMS AND THE LEDGER RECORDS N; no lift was held at a ceiling, so THIS gate's own reading is unchanged').

findings.detail: NEW CLAUSE, AND IT DROPPED THE ONE TOKEN THAT MADE THE PAIRING TRUE. cap.valve's nonpositive prose prints `(CAP_FAB_START={cap.fab_start}, {oe})` -- the lever AND the origin string -- so when the cap came from a checkpoint the reader sees 'CAP_FAB_START=0, checkpoint (lifted to -3)'. The clamp's new clause prints only `{f['lever']}={f['given']}` and drops `{oe}`, so on the restore path it prints a lever value that did not produce the cap: 'the soft cap is -3 (CAP_FAB_START=0)'. CAP_FAB_START=0 is the documented SENTINEL for 'start at the hard ceiling', i.e. the opposite of -3, so the clause reads as an equation between two numbers that are not related. capacity/api.py::_resolve's four origin strings exist precisely so 'a cap that came from the wrong place is visible' (new_valve's own DID IT FIRE block), and this clause is the one surface that now hides it. Reachability is narrow and I state it as I found it: it needs CAP.restore/new_valve(restored=...) to supply a non-positive cap, which the shipped lift arithmetic never produces, so it takes a corrupt or hand-written checkpoint. FIX: carry the origin in the record (`{'cap':ce,'lever':'CAP_FAB_START','given':cap.fab_start,'origin':oe}`) and render `({f['lever']}={f['given']}, {f['origin']})`, exactly as cap.valve does.
